# F9: the SQF command surface {#sec-fg-command-surface}

An SQF command has a name, one or more syntaxes, a return type, an
introduction version and a locality. The engine also carries a command
whitelist and a command disable list. Read the command database page first,
then call the command {src:cmd:selectionNames}.

## What works

The command database holds one page for each command. A page records the
name, the group labels, each syntax alternative, the return type, the
introduction version, the argument locality and the effect locality. AEE
reads the page, not memory {src:cmd:selectionNames}.

`selectionNames` carries two syntax alternatives. The default form reads the
first model level of detail. The second form takes a level of detail name or
resolution and starts at version 2.0. The return type is an array of
selection names. The command itself starts at version 1.58
{src:cmd:selectionNames}.

`setObjectMaterial` takes an object and a `[selectionNumber, material]`
array. The argument locality is global. The effect locality is local. The
return type is Nothing. The command starts at version 0.50
{src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}.

`CfgCommands` declares the command whitelist for the mission.
`CfgDisabledCommands` disables a named command at load
{src:cfg:CfgCommands} {src:cfg:CfgDisabledCommands}.

The database holds 2696 command pages. It assigns each command one or more
of 89 group labels. A command can carry two labels, so the label counts sum
to more than the page count {src:script:tools/arma3-wiki/fetch-wiki.py}.

The source is the acemod arma3-wiki distribution version 2.22, a machine
readable copy of the Bohemia Interactive Community Wiki. The offline reader
fetches one page by name {src:script:tools/arma3-wiki/README.md}.

## What does not work

An undocumented command does not work. The database holds no page, so the
name, the syntax and the version are unknown. The wiki documents the public
surface only, so a missing page is not proof that the engine lacks the
command {src:script:tools/arma3-wiki/README.md}.

A command outside its version range does not work. The database records the
introduction version, and the engine has no command before that version. A
call of `selectionNames` in a build before 1.58 has no result
{src:cmd:selectionNames}.

A client-only command does not work on a dedicated server. `drawIcon3D` has
a local effect and draws to the local game view. A headless server runs no
game view, so the draw has no target {src:cmd:drawIcon3D}. The exe string
table carries the two class names and the disable rule
{src:exe:arma3_x64.exe}.

## Limitations

The database holds 2696 command pages. 2653 pages carry an Arma 3 version.
The remaining 43 pages carry no Arma 3 version, because the command
predates the version field {src:cmd:selectionNames}.

The exe exposes 1802 verb-prefixed command names. The database holds 2696
pages. The two counts measure different sets, so the difference is not a
missing-command count. The exact reconciliation between the two counts is
UNKNOWN against these sources {src:exe:arma3_x64.exe}.

The issue names 74 command groups. The database carries 89 group labels.
The database keeps sub-groups separate, so the labels do not reconcile the
74. The exact 74-group list is UNKNOWN against this source
{src:script:tools/arma3-wiki/fetch-wiki.py}.

## Breaks visually

A disabled command errors at load. `CfgDisabledCommands` removes the
command name, and a script that still calls it stops. The error appears in
the log at start, so the scene loads without the intended result
{src:cfg:CfgDisabledCommands}.

A wrong locality desynchronises the scene. `setObjectMaterial` sets a
global argument and a local effect. When a script expects a local effect on
every machine, the other machines keep the old material. One screen then
shows a part that the other screens do not {src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}.
